item.title: Classrooms destroyed by strong winds
item.description: STRONG winds and rain on Thursday night destroyed six temporary classrooms at the Huonville Primary School in Lae. The sudden strong wind occurred around Lae’s ward two area, causing minor damage to properties, bringing down power poles, with the primary school to bear its full impact. item.title: PM Marape commends Ok Tedi for extending mine life and strengthening national economic security
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has commended the board, management and workforce of Ok Tedi Mining Limited (OTML) for extending the life of the mine to 2084, securing one of Papua New Guinea’s most important national economic assets for future generations. He praised the leadership of the OTML board, managing director and the Chief Executive Officer, Mr Kedi Llimbit, describing the extension as one of the most significant milestones in the country’s resource sector history. item.title: Western Province landowners to secure 40 per cent stake in Ok Tedi Mine
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has announced that landowners in Western Province will be given a 40 per cent equity stake in the Ok Tedi Mine, marking a significant shift in resource ownership in Papua New Guinea’s history. “This is a historic shift that places our people firmly as partners in development,” Marape said, confirming Cabinet’s approval in line with Pangu Pati policy. item.title: MiBank CEO calls for documented land value to unlock credit for PNG farmers
item.description: The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of MiBank, Trudi Egi, has challenged customary landowners to bridge the gap between bankable and unbankable assets to unlock the big demand for credit in Papua New Guinea’s rural sector. In his remarks during a thematic panel on the Customary Land and Human Rights today, Mr. Egi addressed the persistent frustration among farmers who feel financial institutions are not doing enough to support their growth. item.title: One dead, three under restricted supervision at Angau Memorial Hospital
item.description: A viral flu has left one dead on remote Siassi Island in Morobe province, while three others were brought under restricted medical supervision to Angau Memorial Hospital in Lae. Authorities have confirmed that those four patients, including the deceased, contracted the viral flu virus whilst attending a church program on the Siassi Islands. item.title: PNG-Australia partnership promotes school readiness and student access for International Education Day 2026
item.description: The Partnership for Improving Education (PIE) and the National Department of Education (NDoE) reaffirm their joint commitment to ensure every child in Papua New Guinea can enrol, attend, and thrive in school, in honour of this year's International Education Day.
